About Fullscript
 
We’re an industry-leading health technology company on a mission to help people get better. We started in 2011 with one simple idea. Make it easier for practitioners to access the products they trust so they can deliver better care.
 
That simple idea grew into a platform that powers every part of care. Today, more than 125,000 practitioners use Fullscript for clinical insights, lab interpretations, patient analytics, education, and access to high-quality supplements. Over 10 million patients rely on Fullscript to stay connected to their care plans and follow through on treatment.
 
We build tools that make care smarter and more human. Tools that save time, simplify decisions, and help practitioners stay closely connected to the people they care for. When everything they need is in one place, they can focus on what matters most: helping people get better.
 
This is your invitation.
 
Bring your ideas, your grit, and your care for people.
Join us and shape the future of care.


The Mission: Care Mode at Fullscript
Fullscript is evolving from a platform patients use to access care into one that helps them actively follow through on it.
What we call Care Mode is at the center of that evolution. It is designed to create a continuous connection between patients and their care teams—helping patients turn recommendations into sustainable actions while giving practitioners greater visibility into what happens between visits.
Our goal is to close the loop from recommendation → engagement → adherence → outcomes, using technology to deepen the connection between patients and their care teams at scale.
This is not engagement for engagement’s sake. It’s about building thoughtful, trusted experiences that help people take the next right step in their care.
The Role
We’re looking for a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead our Patient Experience pod and help shape the technical and product foundations of Care Mode.
This role blends engineering leadership, product thinking, and people leadership. You’ll stay close to the work—contributing to technical design and implementation, navigating difficult engineering decisions, and stepping in when deeper context or hands-on support is needed—while creating the conditions for a strong team to do its best work.
We believe great engineering leaders are builders at heart. You can zoom out to understand strategy and product intent, then zoom back into the implementation when it matters. You bring clarity to ambiguity, raise the bar through example, and create momentum through trust, context, and shared ownership.
The product reflects the team that builds it. This role shapes both.
What You’ll Do
Build and lead
Cross-functional team on patient experience; set technical direction in a complex, evolving domain.
Stay meaningfully hands-on through system design, code, reviews, prototyping, and solving difficult technical problems.
Set technical direction and evolve architecture in a complex, rapidly developing product domain.
Lead design discussions where product, engineering, data, and clinical considerations intersect.
Own hard problems
Help evolve Fullscript from transactional patient experiences toward a longitudinal, person-centric model of care.
Build systems that bring together clinical data, behavioral signals, and real-world patient context.
Make deliberate tradeoffs across speed, quality, reliability, safety, and trust.
Bring structure and momentum to ambiguous problems without waiting for perfect information.
Raise the bar
Establish a high bar for technical and product quality through how you build, review, and make decisions.
Create an environment that combines psychological safety with meaningful accountability.
Develop engineers through coaching, pairing, feedback, technical debate, and hands-on collaboration.
Continually challenge the team to ask: Are we solving the right problem? Is the experience worthy of the people who depend on us?
Collaborate at scale
Partner closely with Product, Design, Clinical, Data, and Engineering leaders across Fullscript.
Influence broader technical direction as Care Mode and patient experiences become increasingly foundational to the Fullscript platform.
Champion patient trust, practitioner workflows, and long-term system health in product and technical decisions.
How We Expect You to Think
We’re looking for a builder with high agency, strong judgment, and a fundamentally optimistic view of what technology can make possible.
You:
Default to action. When something is unclear, narrow the problem, propose a path, and move — then adjust with data.
Enforce a high bar on reliability and trust: bug discipline, instrumentation, dogfooding. Quality is non-negotiable; so is shipping.
Take ownership beyond the boundaries of your formal scope.
Are comfortable operating in ambiguity and moving forward with incomplete information.
Challenge direction thoughtfully when something doesn’t feel right—and help create a better path.
Care about outcomes, not simply output.
You’re equally comfortable asking “What should we build?” and “How should we build it?”
What You Bring
Significant experience building and leading software products end-to-end, from early concepts through iteration and operation at scale.
Multiple years of engineering management experience, with a clear commitment to people leadership while remaining deeply technical and close to the work.
A track record of owning difficult, non-obvious technical problems with meaningful product and user impact.
Comfort moving between hands-on engineering and engineering leadership—sometimes within the same day.
Strong technical judgment and an ability to communicate why a decision matters, not simply what should be built.
Experience building and operating high-scale applications, with a strong appreciation for reliability, performance, maintainability, and user trust.
Strong product instincts and the ability to connect engineering decisions to the experience they create for users.
Strong signals for this role include:
Deep experience building successful consumer-facing web and/or mobile products, where engagement, retention, usability, and product quality were central to the experience.
Experience building consumer experiences that proactively give users a reason to return—through timely, relevant, personalized, or context-aware interactions that reduce effort and sustain engagement over time.
Fluency with modern AI-assisted engineering workflows and tools, with strong judgment about how to use AI to explore options, challenge assumptions, accelerate implementation, and improve technical decision-making.
Strong instincts around responsiveness, fast feedback loops, perceived performance, and the details that make software feel lightweight and intuitive.
Experience designing for moments when users may be overwhelmed, disengaged, or uncertain about what to do next.
Experience with React, React Native, Rails, GraphQL, Apollo. Specific technologies matter less than depth of technical thinking and craftsmanship.
Bonus signals we value:
Experience building products in regulated, safety-sensitive, or high-trust domains.
A track record of raising quality bars, not simply increasing velocity.
An ability to challenge people constructively and leave teams stronger and more energized as a result.
How We Build
We care deeply about craft, empathy, and trust. Our engineering values are captured in the Fullscript Developer Handbook.
We believe complexity should be clarified rather than surfaced, technology should deepen human care rather than replace it, and great teams outperform lone heroes.
This is an opportunity to help establish how Fullscript builds and engages patients on mobile. You’ll join an experienced team, strong product leadership, and the opportunity to shape the technical approach, product experience, and engineering practices that take it forward. It combines the scope and ambiguity of a new product with the resources and scale of an established company.
What We Can Offer You
Generous PTO and competitive pay
Fullscript’s RRSP match program for financial health
Flexible benefits package and workplace wellness program
Training budget and company-wide learning initiatives
Discount on Fullscript catalog of products
Ability to work Wherever You Work Well*
 
Our Wherever You Work Well philosophy means Fullscript teammates get to pick their own office — whether that’s in-office, at home, or a bit of both 🐶🏡

 The Opportunity 
 The Senior Technical Writer owns documentation for one or more product areas of the Fullscript platform, and partners on the content strategy behind how the Support Center as a whole is structured. It has grown alongside a platform that evolves quickly. Expect a mix of mature documentation to maintain and refine, and newer product surfaces where you decide what should exist at all.
 This role reports to the Manager, Support Documentation, and is a primary partner on content strategy. You are comfortable deciding how content is structured so people can find it, where the line falls between self-service and a conversation with a support agent, which numbers the work should move, and what to stop doing. The work stays hands-on. You will keep writing and editing documentation alongside the structural work.
 The Support Center is the source of truth for platform knowledge, whether the reader is a practitioner, a patient, or one of our own support agents. An error in it reaches every audience at once, and content has to hold up for someone scanning a page as much as for a system pulling a single answer out of it.
 What you'll do 
 Documentation ownership 
 Own the content lifecycle for your product areas, from planning and drafting through maintenance and retirement, across every audience those areas touch.
 Document complex platform behavior, including integrations, identity and permissions, and net-new features with no existing content model to build on.
 Answer the question the reader arrived with, and where it genuinely helps, surface the adjacent capability they did not know existed.
 Use AI-assisted authoring to draft, summarize, and audit, then validate the output against the product before it publishes.
 Information architecture and content strategy 
 Partner with the Manager, Support Documentation, to design and evolve the information architecture of the Support Center: taxonomy, content types, navigation, and the metadata schema underneath them.
 Identify when a new feature makes existing documentation inconsistent or redundant, and lead the consolidation rather than layering new content on top.
 Monitor documentation effectiveness through self-service resolution, search performance, feature adoption, and support contact volume on documented topics, and prioritize work based on what those show.
 Produce AI-ready content: topics that still make sense when a system pulls one out on its own, consistent semantic markup, and metadata complete enough to route a question to the right answer.
 Use insights on where AI-assisted support returns wrong answers to prioritize the content fixes that follow, and negotiate that work against everything else in the queue.
 Release scoping and cross-functional collaboration 
 Gather and validate technical information ahead of a release, partnering with Product Management, Product Marketing, Engineering, and whichever subject matter experts (SMEs) own the detail, and translate what you learn into documentation.
 Work with support managers and frontline agents to find where customers get stuck, and use what they see to decide what gets documented and at what depth. Flag for Product when a pattern points at the product rather than the content.
 Produce an impact assessment for each release: which existing content becomes inaccurate, which audiences are affected, and who owns each open question.
 Identify what readers will need that the product specification does not address, and pursue those questions to an answer rather than documenting around the gap.
 Scope and size the releases nobody else can take yet, flag what will not fit early enough for someone to make a call, and grow the team's scoping until writers handle their own domains unaided.
 Standards, quality, and governance 
 Model and enforce the style guide, editorial policy, and content quality standard, and keep them current as the platform changes.
 Maintain consistent terminology across the Support Center: a controlled vocabulary of approved terms, the variants to avoid, and definitions SMEs have signed off on.
 Improve content operations: templates and content types, SME review and approval workflows, and a review cadence driven by risk, usage, and feedback rather than by article age.
 Govern the entire Support Center, including content the team does not author: taxonomy and metadata consistency, deduplication, and a defined path from published to deprecated to archived with redirects in place.
 Peer review and mentorship 
 Provide peer review and mentorship on craft, and be the editorial resource other writers come to.
 Bring other writers into release scoping and walk them through how you got to the impact assessment.
 What you bring to the table 
 5+ years writing technical or support documentation for SaaS platforms or complex software environments.
 Direct experience changing the structure of a documentation set, knowledge base, or help center, not only working within one.
 Strong writing skills, with the ability to turn complex technical behavior into accurate, scannable documentation, and to write the same information at the right depth for a practitioner, a patient, or a support agent.
 Comfortable working from incomplete information. You can define the documentation plan for a release that is still taking shape instead of waiting for a finished brief.
 Experience with content modeling and single-sourcing, so a fact lives in one place rather than being maintained across a dozen articles.
 Proficiency in a modern content management system, including its structured fields and metadata rather than only its authoring view.
 Comfort with AI-assisted authoring, and an interest in why a well-written article can still produce a wrong answer. 
 Bonus if you have 
 Healthcare, clinical, or other regulated software documentation experience.
 Experience with knowledge management practices where support agents contribute and improve content as they resolve cases.
 Experience improving how content gets found, through on-site search relevance, query analysis, or external ranking.
 Documenting integrations across a partner ecosystem, where behavior differs from one integration to the next.
 Experience with a component content management system (CCMS) such as Paligo, Heretto, or IXIASOFT, or with structured authoring in DITA.
 Taxonomy or ontology work, including knowledge graphs and the entity relationships underneath them.
 Prior work grounding a knowledge base for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or an AI support assistant, including how you measured whether the answers came back right.
 Prompt design, or a working view of where AI-generated drafts reliably fall short. 
 What we can offer you 
 Remote-first flexibility to work where you work best, with Ottawa, Toronto, or Calgary preferred for this role. 
 Flexible PTO and competitive pay, because work-life balance matters 
 RRSP/401k match and competitive compensation packages to invest in your future 
 Premium benefits package with customizable coverage, paramedical services, and an HSA. 
 Fullscript discounts to save on high-quality wellness products 
 Continuous learning opportunities to grow your skills and career
 Compensation range 
 The salary range for this role is between $75,000 and $90,000 (CAD) . Fullscript shares salary ranges to support transparency and help candidates make informed decisions. The range shown reflects base salary only. The range shown reflects base salary only. Additional incentives, perks, and benefits may be available as part of Fullscript’s total rewards package.
Final compensation depends on experience, skills, and location. We review pay regularly to stay aligned with market data and internal equity. Benefits and total rewards may vary by region.
 Why Fullscript 
 Great work happens when people feel supported, trusted, and inspired. At Fullscript, we stay curious and keep finding smarter ways to make care better. We grow together, take on new challenges, and focus on impact. We put people first, work as a team, and leave egos at the door.
 What to Know Before You Apply

The Vice President, Digital runs the commercial operation of the digital channel, turning merchandising, marketing and loyalty offers into activated onsite experiences that make the eCommerce plan achievable. 
 Reporting to the SVP, Digital & Loyalty, accountability spans onsite execution end to end: the merchandising experience, digital assortment and promo activation, online assortment expansion (2P ownership), product content health, and the product data that helps customers discover products, build intent to purchase, and ultimately convert. The mandate is delivered in close partnership with the COO organization. As the primary digital partner to the Banner Presidents and merchandising teams, the VP translates banner and category plans into onsite execution. 
 The position also owns how customers find Canadian Tire in a changing discovery landscape. As search shifts from traditional engines to answer engines, generative surfaces and agentic shopping assistants, this role leads the SEO, AEO and GEO agenda — from early experimentation to scaled, repeatable practice. The VP is a key stakeholder in the True North eCommerce Accelerate strategy, shaping business requirements that Digital Product teams can translate into new capabilities across the digital commerce ecosystem, including Digital Harmonization, 2P and Digital Experience Drivers. 
 What You'll Do   
 Digital Merchandising   
 Own the onsite merchandising experience across homepage, category pages, navigation and onsite search relevance.  
 Own digital assortment presentation and promo execution onsite, aligned to banner, category and enterprise promo plans.  
 Ensure marketing, merchandising and loyalty offers are activated consistently across the websites and the CTR app.  
 Surface the right products earlier in the shopping journey, converting discovery into considered intent to purchase.  
 Partner with Pricing & Promo and Brand & Marketing so onsite execution reflects the enterprise promotional calendar and price architecture.  
 Serve as the senior digital partner to Banner Presidents and category teams, translating their plans into a clear onsite execution plan with visible trade-offs where capacity is constrained.  
 Digital Analytics & Activation   
 Act as the key owner driving the agentic commerce ambition forward — defining how CTC's assortment, content and offers are surfaced to AI shopping assistants and agent-mediated journeys.  
 Lead the AEO and GEO agenda alongside SEO, treating traditional and AI-driven discovery as one connected practice.  
 Own onsite performance analytics, including KPI definition, competitive benchmarking and the digital measurement fact base used in commercial decisions.  
 Build the measurement approach for AI-driven discovery — visibility, citation, referral quality and downstream intent to purchase — and use it to steer investment.  
 Run the digital activation and experimentation practice, converting test wins into standing site practice rather than one-off lifts.  
 Own the digital performance management rhythm: KPI reporting, performance reviews and early escalation of risks to the outlook.  
 Partner with IT on the technical integrations required for search, LLM and agentic discoverability.  
 Digital Content Operations   
 Own onsite content health across copy, imagery and specification accuracy, at the quality standard the banners expect.  
 Own content grooming and meta tagging so customers can discover our products across search, generative and agentic surfaces.  
 Ensure product content answers the questions that drive purchase decisions, building customer confidence and intent at the point of discovery.  
 Run vendor product data onboarding, data quality and bilingual compliance, scaling throughput as assortment expands.  
 Set the structured data and content standards that allow customers — and the assistants acting for them — to discover our products and understand why to choose them.  
 Product Content Capabilities   
 Own the content platform agenda across Product 2.0 including PIM, PCM and DAM, defining the operational requirements that the roadmap must satisfy.  
 Drive product process automation and AI-assisted rules that scale onboarding without scaling headcount.  
 Lead a team of product managers and manage IT delivery of new capability and ongoing support.  
 Partner with Digital Product on roadmap sequencing so capability lands against real category and banner plans.  
 Online Assortment (2P)   
 Serve as the True North 2P initiative lead, accountable for the initiative's direction, milestones and reported outcomes.  
 Build the 2P assortment expansion agenda — onboarding, content readiness and onsite presentation at scale.  
 Connect 2P growth to the broader discoverability agenda so expanded assortment is surfaced to customers and AI-driven discovery alike.  
 Represent 2P progress, risks and trade-offs in True North governance and enterprise forums.  
 Team & Leadership   
 Lead a multi-disciplinary team spanning digital merchandising, analytics and activation, content operations and content management products.  
 Build capability and bench strength across the function, with clear accountability at the AVP level and a deliberate approach to vacancy and succession risk.  
 Set a performance culture grounded in evidence, speed and commercial ownership.  
 What You Bring   
 Senior leadership experience in eCommerce, digital commerce or omni-channel retail, with the ability to operate as a peer to senior commercial, banner and merchandising leaders.  
 A proven record of delivering commercial results through digital execution, onsite activation and measurable customer experience improvements in a large, multi-banner retail environment.  
 Depth across digital merchandising, onsite search, digital analytics and experimentation, product content operations, and AI-enabled discovery practices including SEO, AEO and GEO.  
 Experience leading enterprise initiatives end to end, including 2P, Digital Harmonization or similar scaled capability programs, with clear governance, milestone and reporting accountability.  
 Strength translating commercial strategy and banner priorities into clear business requirements that Digital Product and Technology teams can convert into new capabilities.  
 Strong people leadership, including building high-performing teams, developing leaders and setting a culture of evidence-based decision making, speed and commercial ownership.

Botpress is the AI agent platform for customer support. We build AI agents that resolve tickets instead of just answering them, for support teams carrying real conversation volume. Our mission is to make AI work for the people doing the work.
 About the Role 
 We are anchoring on a sales-led motion, and this role makes it repeatable. The most important problem in the company right now is building pipeline with new accounts that fit. You will own the marketing half of it: demand for larger accounts, up to enterprise, through experimentation and a multi-channel approach.
 We’ll be honest about the stage. The product can do a lot, we know who we’re for, and we’re still learning which channels bring those people in predictably. You’ll have a few channels to run with some predictability and a handful of experiments at any time. You’ll be expected to stop what doesn’t work, and to say so early.
 Responsibilities 
 Events: private invite-only events, and how we show up around the big industry conferences (our own dinners and rooms alongside them). Marketing leads, Sales brings the people in the room. You will have resources to help execute, but you own and lead the vision: where we show up, why, and who we want at the table.
 Direct mail and gifting
 ABM programs: the plays against the named-account list, from first touch to the hand-off into Sales
 Paid media, through our agency or in house, on a small budget that has to prove itself one play at a time in order to scale
 The marketing inputs to our outbound engine: targeting, segments, messaging and the content the sequences use. You own the list and the outreach alongside our team of BDRs.
 The acquisition experiment portfolio: what we test, in what order, and what we learn
 The agencies and vendors behind these channels: the brief, the budget, and the call to keep, cut or bring in-house
 Your first 90 days 
 Improve our paid ads impact
 Launch an invite-only / in person AI workshop for target accounts
 Experiment with a direct mail campaign
 Make the keep-or-bring-in-house call on our outbound vendor
 Build the first ABM plays against the named-account list, with the CRO and Sales
 Get the podcast, the events and the outbound list working as one multi-threaded motion, so a good-fit account hears from us more than once
 Curious, and able to step back. You follow threads: why, what would prove it, what is the smallest way to test it. You can reflect strategically and form a point of view. Then you ship the experiment anyway.
 High follow-through. You are a doer. Things you start get finished, and you close the loop without being chased.
 A doer who delegates. You cover more ground by handing work to agencies, freelancers, agents and teammates, and by briefing them well.
 80/20 by instinct. You find the few things with the biggest impact and start there. More is not better. We test the minimum viable version of a play before we invest in the full one.
 Deep in one channel, willing to wing the others. Maybe you are a paid expert. You will still need to build an event play and a direct mail play from scratch, and we want someone who is happy to.
 You lean on AI heavily. It is the motto of the team and the company, and it is part of the interview. Tell us how you would enhance the team with your AI thinking, processes and agents. If you don’t lean on it heavily, this role isn’t for you.
 Evidence and instinct, in balance. You read the numbers, and you also trust your read of a room, an account, a message. You can say which one you used and why.
 Intellectual humility. You are quick to say “I was wrong, here is what changed my mind.” We will ask you about a failure you are genuinely proud of, and about something you built that you are slightly embarrassed by.
 The team you’d join 
 A small, senior, hands-on marketing team. Growth and product-led growth, SEO and AEO and content, brand and design, and product marketing. Paid and outbound run through agencies you will manage. The team scales with AI, not headcount, by design: people build their own skills and agents on our own platform, and every other week we run a Marketing AI Open Hour where someone shows what they built. You would be joining people who ship, and who expect you to show your own work too.
 Why join this team 
 You report to the VP Growth/Marketing, who gives a lot of feedback and builds it into the job: a monthly reflection 1:1, a coaching check-in every two months, and feedback that is specific, early and visible. We move fast and there is no ego. We take 100% responsibility for outcomes, with curiosity instead of blame. We use evidence and instinct, and we try AI before we add people. You get the chance to build the acquisition engine for a sales-led motion, not inherit one.
 Who you work with 
 Day to day you work with the CRO and the sales team. You also work with our partner lead, our design lead, and the agencies you manage.
 The BDR team sits in Sales, and you own the list and the outreach alongside them. Which accounts we go after is decided together by Marketing, Sales and the CEO.
 Work with a talented and passionate team
 4 weeks of vacation
 Paid sick and parental leave
 Comprehensive health, dental, vision, travel, and life insurance
 Funding for education and skills improvement
 Fully-stocked fridge and cupboard – we take snacks seriously
 A meaningful stock option grant — we want everyone at Botpress to think and act as an owner, and to share in what we build
 RRSP program
 A vibrant office community

 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 · Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.

 · Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique.
 · Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui fait une place de choix à l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite.
 · Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur.
 · Investissement dans la collectivité : Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale.
 Aperçu de l’équipe 
 · Dirigé par le chef des services informatiques, le Groupe des solutions numériques et technologiques a vu le jour en 2023 afin de donner à nos clients et à nos employés les outils nécessaires pour conquérir le monde en offrant de façon cohérente des services numériques fiables et sécurisés. Ses objectifs sont les suivants :
 o Définir, instaurer et maintenir l’état cible en matière de technologie intégrée, le modèle de données cibles et les activités technologiques nécessaires à la transformation opérationnelle d’EDC d’ici 2030.
 o Créer et gérer la feuille de route numérique continue sur trois ans; ce document établit l’ordre d’obtention des résultats requis pour atteindre l’état cible en matière de technologie et en facilite la mise en œuvre dans tous les secteurs de l’organisation.
 o Demeurer au fait des tendances sectorielles et des technologies émergentes pour qu’EDC dispose des outils numériques qui assureront sa pertinence sur le marché et lui permettront d’accroître la présence commerciale du Canada sur la scène internationale.
 o Voir à la mise en œuvre intégrée des projets sur le plan du numérique, des données, des infrastructures et de la cybersécurité afin d’offrir une excellente expérience aux clients, aux utilisateurs et aux employés.
 Ce que vous ferez: 
 La personne choisie se joindra à l’Escouade de l’assurance, qui fait partie du Groupe de l’exécution et de l’architecture de la plateforme numérique.
 Elle définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies d’essai qui garantiront la qualité, la fiabilité et le bon fonctionnement des logiciels organisationnels. Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, la personne choisie dirigera les e ssais manuels et automatisés et assumera la responsabilité des cadres connexes, des outils et des résultats probants d’une ou de plusieurs initiatives en matière de TI.
 La personne choisie assurera la conception, la mise en œuvre et la maintenance des solutions d’essai automatisées, intégrera une composante d’essai dans le cycle de développement logiciel et travaillera de concert avec les développeurs, les responsables de produits et les équipes de déploiement à repérer, puis corriger les défauts. Elle jouera un rôle de premier plan dans la fiabilité de la qualité du déploiement, l’atténuation du risque de régression et l’accélération de la mise en ligne de versions de qualité.
 Principales responsabilités 
 1. Définir et exécuter des stratégies et des plans d’essai conformes à l’architecture de solutions, aux échéanciers et aux objectifs en matière de qualité pour toutes les initiatives de TI sous sa gouverne.
 2. Concevoir, rédiger et appliquer des cas d’essai manuels et automatisés qui vérifient la conformité aux exigences fonctionnelles (et certaines non fonctionnelles), d’intégration et de régression.
 3. Concevoir, implanter et tenir à jour des cadres et des scripts d’essai d’automatisation qui sont hautement pertinents, reproductibles et fondés sur le risque.
 4. Intégrer les essais automatisés dans le développement logiciel et les cycles d’intégration continue ou de déploiement continu afin d’assurer une mise à l’essai constante et une détection précoce des défauts.
 5. Relever, consigner, suivre et retester les défauts , en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de développement logiciel, pour assurer une résolution rapide et des résultats optimaux.
 6. Soutenir et valider les essais d’acceptation par l’utilisateur en faisant concorder les résultats des essais avec les exigences opérationnelles, de concert avec les utilisateurs fonctionnels, et en veillant à ce que les problèmes soient bien compris, hiérarchisés et résolus.
 7. Collaborer avec des parties prenantes provenant de diverses équipes de déploiement et sectorielles (développeurs, responsables de produits, chefs de mêlée, testeurs fonctionnels) pour assurer une certaine qualité tout au long du processus de déploiement agile et faire un suivi de l’avancement des essais, des risques et des indicateurs de qualité.
 Ce que nous cherchons:

 · Au moins 5 années d’expérience dans l’automatisation des tests d’assurance qualité ou dans le développement de logiciels
 · Au moins 5 années d’expérience de la mise à l’essai d’applications Web : expérience avérée de la mise à l’essai d’applications Web, y compris les essais fonctionnels, de convivialité, de sécurité et de rendement
 · Au moins 3 années d’expérience dans la mise à l’essai des services dorsaux (API) et des points d’intégration de l’application
 · Au moins 2 années d’expérience dans un environnement agile
 · Connaissance approfondie des principes et des pratiques de développement de systèmes de TI
 · Excellentes compétences en résolution de problèmes et en communication
 · Expérience avec Azure DevOps, Jira ou tout autre outil de gestion des exigences ou des défauts
 Ce qui vous distinguera:

 · Connaissance de la gestion de bases de données et du langage SQL pour tester les applications de base de données et vérifier l’intégrité des données
 · Expérience du développement de codes en utilisant l’IA, notamment GitHub Copilot
 · Expérience de la programmation avec Python et Robot Framework
 · Expérience avec PostMan
 · Compétences en programmation ou en écriture de scripts dans des langages tels que Python, Java, Selenium
 · Expérience des pipelines pour l’intégration continue et le déploiement continu
 Admissibilité

Le poste est ouvert aux personnes qui répondent à toutes les exigences essentielles énoncées ci-dessus et dont la candidature est reçue avant la date limite.
 Engagement d’EDC envers l’équité en matière d’emploi 
 Exportation et développement Canada (EDC) s’engage à favoriser l’équité en matière d’emploi et à constituer une main-d’œuvre diversifiée. Elle s’engage à créer un environnement sûr et inclusif qui respecte les personnes de toutes les origines, aptitudes et compétences. EDC favorise une culture d’inclusion et d’appartenance où chaque personne a des chances égales de se perfectionner, de se développer, de réussir et de réaliser son plein potentiel. 
 EDC invite les femmes, les Autochtones, les membres d’une minorité visible, les personnes en situation de handicap et les membres de la communauté 2ELGBTQI+ à poser leur candidature. 
 Votre candidature doit démontrer clairement que vous répondez à toutes les exigences. Nous remercions l’ensemble des candidates et candidats de leur intérêt pour une carrière à EDC. Toutefois, seules les personnes sélectionnées pour un entretien seront contactées. Veuillez noter que les candidates et les candidats qualifiés peuvent être pris en considération pour des postes similaires à ce niveau au sein d’EDC. 
 EDC reconnaît que le fait de divulguer la nécessité de prévoir des mesures d’adaptation peut être une question personnelle. Sachez qu’en tant qu’organisation, nous nous engageons à respecter la confidentialité et à veiller à ce que toutes les mesures d’adaptation fournies soient adaptées à vos besoins. Notre objectif est de vous garantir une expérience positive et satisfaisante tout au long du processus de recrutement. N’hésitez donc pas à communiquer directement avec nous pour toute demande d’adaptation à l’adresse accessibility@edc.ca . Nous sommes là pour vous aider à chaque étape du processus. 
 Énoncé de confidentialité 
 En posant votre candidature pour ce poste, vous reconnaissez avoir lu et compris l’ Énoncé de confidentialité à l’intention des demandeurs d’emploi d’EDC , qui décrit notre processus de collecte, d’utilisation, de conservation et de protection des renseignements personnels au cours du processus de recrutement, ainsi que vos droits d’accès et de correction.

 Introduction to the Role :
 The CMC Regulatory Affairs, Submissions & Operations role is responsible for the hands-on execution and coordination of CMC regulatory activities across assigned programs. This role reports into the Associate Director, CMC Regulatory Affairs and partners closely with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure regulatory deliverables are developed, reviewed, tracked, and submitted accurately and on time.
 The role is highly execution-focused and requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, regulatory knowledge, and the ability to manage multiple concurrent deliverables. The successful candidate will be comfortable working within regulatory systems and submission processes while maintaining a strong understanding of the broader CMC regulatory objectives of each program.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Regulatory Submission Execution 
 Coordinate and execute CMC regulatory submission activities across development and commercial programs.
 Lead the development and authoring of complex CMC regulatory documents and submission content.
 Translate complex CMC and scientific information into clear, concise, scientifically sound regulatory narratives.
 Support preparation and compilation of CMC content for IND/CTA, NDA/BLA/MAA, supplements/variations, annual reports, and other regulatory submissions as applicable.
 Coordinate submission deliverables across CMC, Quality, Manufacturing, Analytical, Regulatory, and other functional teams.
 Track document development, review cycles, approvals, and submission readiness.
 Ensure CMC regulatory documents are completed according to established timelines and quality standards.
 Support responses to health authority questions and requests for information.
 Regulatory Systems & Submission Operations 
 Execute activities within the Enterprise Regulatory Vault (ERV) and other applicable regulatory systems.
 Maintain accurate submission records, metadata, document status, and regulatory correspondence.
 Coordinate document filing and archival activities in accordance with applicable processes.
 Support publishing, submission assembly, document formatting, and technical submission requirements.
 Ensure regulatory information and documentation remain accurate, current, and inspection-ready.
 Responsibility for change management as assigned
 Understands application of appropriate risk management across own activities
 Project & Workflow Management 
 Maintain CMC regulatory submission trackers, timelines, action logs, and deliverable plans.
 Proactively identify upcoming milestones, dependencies, and potential delays.
 Coordinate meetings, agendas, actions, and follow-up activities related to CMC regulatory deliverables.
 Escalate risks and issues to the Associate Director, CMC Regulatory Affairs or functional lead.
 Support multiple programs and submissions simultaneously while effectively prioritizing competing deadlines.
 CMC Regulatory Content Support 
 Draft, Author, Review CMC regulatory documents for completeness, consistency, formatting, and alignment with submission requirements.
 Support preparation and review of CMC regulatory documents and submission components.
 Coordinate cross-functional review and incorporation of comments.
 Maintain consistency of CMC information across regulatory documents and submissions.
 Develop and maintain submission templates, trackers, checklists, and other operational tools.
 Process Improvement 
 Identify opportunities to improve CMC regulatory submission processes, systems, and workflows.
 Contribute to development and implementation of standardized processes and best practices.
 Support continuous improvement of regulatory systems, document management, and submission execution.
 Promote efficient, consistent, and compliant ways of working across CMC Regulatory Affairs.
 Health Authority Questions & Responses 
 Drive CMC Regulatory Affairs activities related to Health Authority Questions (HAQs), information requests, and other post-submission regulatory correspondence.
 Assess HAQs from a regulatory and scientific perspective and develop an appropriate response strategy.
 Conduct cross-functional meetings to clarify questions, establish ownership, align on interpretation, and agree on response strategy and key messages.
 Partner with CMC subject matter experts to develop scientifically robust and regulatory-appropriate responses.
 Draft responses to complex or high-priority HAQs, and drive through the review workflow to endorsement/approval and delivery.
 Coordinate cross-functional review and ensure responses are accurate, consistent, complete, and aligned with the overall regulatory strategy.
 Provide regulatory assessment of proposed responses and identify potential follow-up questions, risks, or regulatory implications.
 Ensure responses are delivered within agreed timelines and meet applicable regulatory requirements.
 Track and compile HAQs across programs to create a database of questions to pull for future requests.
 Track commitments made to regulatory agencies based on HAQs
 Qualifications & Experience 
 Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific, regulatory, or related discipline.
 Experience in Regulatory Affairs, preferably CMC Regulatory Affairs within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or related industry.
 Demonstrated experience supporting or executing regulatory submissions.
 Strong understanding of regulatory submission processes and documentation requirements.
 Experience working within regulatory information/document management systems; experience with Enterprise Regulatory Vault (ERV) is an asset.
 Strong organizational and project coordination skills with exceptional attention to detail.
 Ability to manage multiple deliverables and timelines in a fast-paced, matrix environment.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams and independently manage assigned responsibilities.
 A proactive, solutions-oriented approach to identifying and resolving operational issues.
 Success in This Role 
 Success in this role means turning regulatory plans into high-quality, timely execution. The successful candidate will be highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable owning the operational details that enable CMC regulatory submissions and activities to run smoothly.
 The role is particularly suited to someone who enjoys getting things done, keeping complex workflows moving, and ensuring that no submission detail falls through the cracks.

 AstraZeneca’s Safety Epidemiology team is a global group of PhD-trained pharmacoepidemiologists with expertise in conducting epidemiological studies, performing evidence synthesis and analytics to evaluate drug safety. The team plans and delivers R&D safety epidemiology activities that inform the benefit–risk profiles of nearly 100 marketed and pipeline products. These activities include local and global post-authorisation regulatory commitment studies (PARCS) submitted to health authorities such as the FDA and EMA. 
 Safety Epidemiology offers a dynamic, inclusive and supportive environment where epidemiologists can build rewarding careers and make meaningful contributions to drug development, pharmacoepidemiology and public health. We welcome applications from recent PhD graduates and postdoctoral researchers in epidemiology who are interested in drug safety, real-world data analysis and a career in the pharmaceutical industry. 
 The quantitative pharmacoepidemiologist role will report to the Senior Director, Safety Epidemiology and is a pivotal scientific role within Global Patient Safety, accountable for performing rapid analyses of large electronic healthcare databases from around the world to support PARCS planning, signal detection, predictive clinical safety, clinical trial planning, drug development, new drug applications to regulatory authorities and to support responses to health authorities (e.g., FDA , EMA etc). 
 The incumbent will be responsible for delivering high-quality descriptive epidemiological analyses of real-world healthcare data across various products in the AZ portfolio. The role applies analytical methods to generate robust evidence from electronic healthcare databases and collaborates with multidisciplinary teams to address scientific and business questions. Key responsibilities include programmatic specification of a research question, analytical study execution, data interpretation, programming, evidence generation, and communication of findings to internal collaborators across Global Patient Safety, Global Regulatory, Global Medical/Clinical functions.

 Ph.D. in pharmacoepidemiology, epidemiology, public health, biostatistics or related health science field and substantial hands-on experience analysing large electronic healthcare data (relational databases) and other real world data sources (claims, registry or other secondary healthcare databases)

 A strong interest in pursuing a career in pharmacoepidemiology and drug safety 
 Able to apply epidemiological theory and techniques to solve new and challenging problems 
 Conceptual understanding of real-world data for secondary research use, and the data generation mechanism that impact how such data is analysed 
 Ability to translate a research question into an implementable query that can be run in a real-world database 
 A strong interest in data management and using data to improve health within the pharmaceutical industry 
 Able to work effectively with internal & external collaborators, including collaborative groups and contract research organizations (CROs) 
 Desirable Requirements 
 PhD dissertation in pharmacoepidemiology or epidemiology with a strong focus on medicines as the exposure of interest

 Hands-on experience planning, analysing and interpreting results of statistical analyses performed using large electronic healthcare data or other real-world data 
 An approach passionate about using imperfect data and finding practical ways to move forward in addressing research objectives

 Working knowledge of epidemiological methods used in research in drug development or in a closely related academic research area

Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik, Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. We’re looking for a versatile, persistent product engineer who’s not afraid to set up reusable building blocks across the stack and advocate for the time and space to do so. At Ashby, all our engineers ship features end-to-end at a high pace. Example is the best leadership. We’ll give you the room to do your best work, and you'll be our guide! If that speaks to you, read on.

What Ashby gives you in return is the best of both early and growth-stage environments. The agency and no-nonsense of a seed startup: you write product specs, make product and design decisions, and build in an almost-no-meeting culture. While also the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup: 100,000+ weekly active users who depend on your software and eagerly await your next feature.

We have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet.

You’ve probably seen this role posted before, and it’s because we’re always expanding the team (we’re on track to double Engineering this year). We’re bubbling with ideas for how to support Talent Acquisition with software, and we recently launched Talent Management products https://www.ashbyhq.com/add-ons/people-workflows to expand our total addressable market and become a company worth $60B+.

We read every application and aim to respond to yours within 3-4 days (often sooner).

 


ABOUT THE ROLE AND HOW WE WORK

Our engineering culture strives to recreate the environments where we did our best work as ICs – where we had the ownership and agency to impact our users with creative and innovative software.

I started my career building software for artists in the Visual Effects industry. It was a formative experience for me as a software engineer because success relied on my ability to be a product manager and designer. I talked to artists to understand their needs. I came up with ideas. I did industry research, designed interfaces, and prototyped ideas. I watched artists use what I built and decided what to tackle in the next iteration. No daily stand-ups, no t-shirt sizing, no planning meetings.

I studied computer science to solve problems, not tickets, and this felt exactly like that. I not only felt creative and fulfilled but the agency and ownership we were given as engineers powered an incredible amount of innovation.

Innovation came differently (or not at all) at technology startups beyond the seed stage, often through an engineer’s force of will and ability to push back against culture (rather than any encouragement from it). Engineering was narrowed to implementation and delivery, partly due to the influence of other departments and partly due to the influx of "Agile" processes like sprint planning. In those companies, I felt like a JIRA jockey. 

At Ashby, we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve. An environment that embraces innovative engineers, and, frankly, often stays out of their way. As a Product Engineer, you’ll take ownership over a large portion of one of our products and own projects end-to-end (wearing hats traditionally worn by product and design). You’ll research competitors, write product specs, make wireframes, and more. To ground it with examples, product engineers at Ashby have:

 - Designed and built automated interview scheduling. This feature automates scheduling by calculating possible times from a pool of interviewers and other constraints, and then presenting these times to the candidate for selection via our responsive web app. This solves the “Calendar Tetris” problem I talk about in "What We're Building."

 - Built a generalized declarative filter architecture that allows users to create complex filters for any record with a consistent UI and compile it to SQL in our backend. Many user-facing features use it.

 - Specced, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to complete signing offers entirely within Ashby. This project involved talking to customers to understand their requirements, deciding what technologies to use, building a prototype, and working with other team members to integrate the final implementation into additional features.

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition (TA) software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

 


WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY

Software engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some things  to help you decide if this fits you and what you’re looking for:

 - You’re not afraid to tackle any part of a technology stack. You do what’s necessary to successfully deliver a feature, whether writing frontend or choosing new infrastructure. We’ll provide a supportive environment to do it successfully (e.g., design system, SRE team).

 - You’ve tackled projects with a lot of product and technical ambiguity, and you thrive at the intersection of the two. We’re not building a simple CRUD app, and many of the challenges we tackle require you to use your knowledge of our customers to build powerful abstractions and flexibility in the system to solve a class of problems.

 - You know how to strike the right balance between speed and quality. Ashby wasn’t built quickly. We took four years to launch publicly because convincing customers to switch required a high-quality product. However, time isn’t infinite, especially for a startup, so we still move with urgency—we’ve built the equivalent of three or more VC-backed startups with a very small team.

 - You are ambitious and always looking to improve your skills. For most engineers, this role will give you more freedom and responsibilities than you’ve experienced in the past. To thrive (and level up), you’ll need to be open to feedback (and we give lots of it).

 - You’re an excellent collaborator and communicator. Ownership and freedom don’t mean you work in a vacuum. You’ll need to vet your decisions with the appropriate stakeholders, keep them up to date when necessary, and work with other engineers to get your projects across the finish line. Clear and concise communication helps a lot here!

 - You seek to create leverage in your work. The nature of software is that you can often automate or abstract what would be tedious, time-consuming work. Your impatience usually leads to new abstractions, tools to allow Support to debug before Engineering, new lint rules to prevent common bugs, etc. 

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:

 - To you, a tech lead, staff, or principal engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews. Our most tenured engineers spend most of their time building, and we often trust them with our most challenging problems. While they lead product and technical areas and help other engineers plan their most challenging work, it’s not a requirement, nor do engineers need their sign-off.

 - You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the technical details and challenges.

 - You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

 - You can get lost in the details. Once you start implementation, it can be hard to take a step back and think about the project as a whole. You like everything to be planned upfront.

 - You haven’t led or taken ownership of projects before. You’re used to working with tech leads and taking on tasks distributed by them.

 - You want to mentor earlier-career engineers. We rely on engineers owning their projects, so we need engineers with that experience. This requires the team to be reasonably tenured. More than 90% of the team would be considered Senior or above in the industry today, so mentorship opportunities are very limited.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/d4679311-9dba-4031-bf5e-19ce78597ab1/calendar.png]
 

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

 


INCREASE LEVERAGE, NOT TEAM SIZE

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

 - Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 - Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 - AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/ai-ashby-engineering-and-the-future.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8d94727a-46d8-42a2-9627-ddcd7f822f95/arjun.png]
 

And a demo of one of these building blocks:




PUT EFFORT INTO DIVERSITY

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 


WORK-LIFE BALANCE: IT’S A MARATHON, NOT A SPRINT

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school.  Mujda https://www.linkedin.com/in/mujdaalamzai/ (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article https://nextplayso.substack.com/p/should-you-join-ashby about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via pair programming, writing product and tech specs collaboratively, and talking through decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

 1. Introduction call with Hiring Manager (15 to 30m, live)

 2. A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)

 3. Three non-coding interviews that focus on product thinking, technical design, and infrastructure (3h 15m, live can be split across multiple days)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

Your hiring manager will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect (you’ll need minimal preparation). You’ll meet 4 to 6 people in engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

 


YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

 


TECHNOLOGY STACK

I’m sharing our tech stack with the caveat that we don’t require previous experience in it (but a love of typed languages is helpful 😀): TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, Redis.

When they joined Ashby, many of our engineers switched from other languages like Swift and Kotlin (Ben https://linkedin.com/in/benasher44/), platforms like iOS (Tom https://www.linkedin.com/in/tom-quist-0925a199/) and Windows (Adam https://www.linkedin.com/in/adam-lusch/). We care more about fundamentals (e.g., debugging, abstractions) and how fast you learn. For folks on the team who switched, it's nice seeing changes hot reload versus waiting for XCode to compile 😅.

 


BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

 Job Description 
 Visa Direct is a fast-growing money movement service that enables Visa clients, including issuers, acquirers, processors, merchants, remitters and service providers, to facilitate domestic and cross-border fund transfers and disbursements to cards, accounts and wallets. Visa Direct uses push payment technology, including Original Credit Transaction (OCT), and relevant account and real-time payment rails to support a broad range of consumer and business use cases, including person-to-person transfer, cross-border remittances, marketplace payouts, royalty and digital content payouts, gig economy services and other business-to-consumer or small business payment flows.
 We are seeking a Director, Visa Direct Account Management Sales, to help manage and grow Visa Direct with key money movement partners in the Canadian market. The role will focus on deepening client relationships, identifying and executing growth opportunities, building sales pipeline, and helping clients expand routes, corridors, use cases and endpoints that drive transaction volume, revenue and Visa share.
 The successful candidate will directly manage a portfolio of assigned client accounts, which may include financial institutions, credit unions, fintech's, remitters and other strategic partners. The Director will work closely with Client Account Executives, Visa Direct product and commercialization teams, pricing, legal, risk, compliance, marketing, client services, finance and regional teams to advance client priorities and support program growth from opportunity identification through launch, ramp, optimization and renewal.
 This is a client-facing role that requires strong commercial judgment, account management discipline, consultative selling skills, organizational savvy and comfort working in a matrixed environment. The ideal candidate is a structured, analytical and proactive sales professional with experience growing payment or money movement relationships, influencing cross-functional stakeholders and translating complex solutions into clear client value.
 Responsibilities:
 The Director, Visa Direct Account Management Sales, is accountable for delivering growth across assigned Visa Direct client accounts in Canada and contributing to the broader Canadian Visa Direct portfolio strategy. The role is responsible for managing client relationships, developing account plans, building pipeline, advancing sales opportunities and driving initiatives that increase transaction volume, revenue, use case adoption and program performance.
 The individual will apply sound commercial judgment to evaluate opportunities, recommend the right path of action, coordinate internal resources and help bring growth initiatives to market. The Director will work across product, pricing, rules, marketing, legal, compliance, risk, finance, client services, operations and regional teams to support technology readiness, corridor expansion, pricing or rule changes, authorization performance, network optimization and lifecycle management across pre-launch, launch, ramp, growth and optimization phases.

 Responsibilities include:
 Account and portfolio growth
 Accountable for assigned account revenue and transaction growth by delivering client growth targets and supporting broader Canadian portfolio objectives across routes, corridors, use cases and endpoints.
 Achieve and exceed account transaction and revenue targets for Visa Direct clients under management, including building clear plans to increase transaction volume, revenue and Visa share.
 Develop and manage account strategies that identify high-potential use cases, marketing opportunities, commercialization priorities and growth acceleration levers.
 Set and track client-specific performance goals by product, use case and enablement milestones, including new endpoints, corridor expansion and program optimization priorities.
 Sales pipeline development and commercialization
 Build and manage sales pipeline across endpoint options, routes, corridors, use cases and value-added services within primary and extended client lines of business.
 Lead or support new and renewal deal activity including opportunity identification, solutioning, business case development, incentives, negotiation and contracting in partnership with internal stakeholders.
 Manage clients through the sales cycle from opportunity development through launch, ramp and ongoing optimization.
 Maintain disciplined opportunity tracking and reporting for accounts under management, including pipeline status, risks, next steps and expected financial impact.
 Client relationship management
 Establish trusted working relationships with clients to understand their business strategy, money movement priorities and operating model.
 Partner with Client Account Executives to define account priorities, align on annual transaction and revenue plans and advance prioritized strategic milestones.
 Engage senior client stakeholders as appropriate with clear, credible and commercially relevant communication on Visa Direct opportunities and performance.
 Work with Marketing to ensure client-facing materials are clear, compelling, on-message and effective in accelerating client understanding and adoption.
 Cross-functional execution
 Partner with Visa Direct commercialization teams to identify go-to-market needs and ensure the right value proposition, product construct and client solution are in place.
 Collaborate with Finance and leadership on forecasting, performance tracking and monthly or quarterly reporting for accounts under management.
 Work with Legal, Risk, Compliance and Pricing to support client contracts, governance requirements and commercial structures that drive successful outcomes for Visa and clients.
 Coordinate with Client Services and product teams to monitor program health, address production issues and recommend optimization opportunities.
 Program performance and optimization
 Actively investigate and manage account program performance with a bias toward resolving issues quickly and completely.
 Analyze dashboards and identify performance trends bringing in product, client services and subject matter experts as needed to address issues and identify growth opportunities.
 Support transaction yield optimization including price, FX and underperforming program revenue impact, in partnership with relevant internal teams.
 Identify and raise product feature enhancements based on client feedback, market needs and account growth priorities.
 Account planning and business reviews
 Develop and maintain account plans for assigned clients, including transaction and revenue targets, strategic priorities, milestones, risks and dependencies.
 Provide insightful program performance reviews that identify growth opportunities, define action plans and support client engagement.
 Lead regular account review and opportunity-solving sessions with cross-functional teams to unblock stalled programs or accelerate growth where transaction volume has plateaued.
 Contribute to Canadian and North America Visa Direct reporting by sharing account progress, pipeline updates, risks and priorities through established internal mechanisms.
 Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.   
 Qualifications

 10 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 8 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters/ MBA/JD/MD) or at least 3 years of work experience with a PhD

 Analytical mindset with comfort using dashboards, performance data and financial metrics to identify trends, issues and optimization opportunities.
 Creative self-starter who is comfortable operating independently, prioritizing across multiple accounts and escalating issues appropriately at critical junctures.

 Passion for transforming payments and excitement about helping grow Visa Direct in Canada.

The Role
 AI Builder Experience (ABX) is MongoDB’s front door for the agentic era. We help human developers and coding agents discover, evaluate, and choose MongoDB, and we make MongoDB work naturally inside the AI-native tools, frameworks, and platforms where software is being built.
 We are looking for an outstanding Staff Product Manager to own the Partner Platform: the products, experiences, and operating model that allow ecosystem partners to build trusted, high-quality MongoDB experiences for their users. This includes the Partner API and the broader path toward self-serve integrations, partner onboarding, enterprise controls, marketplace/discovery, and partner-managed experiences.
 This is a role at the intersection of humans, machines, and partners. Human builders increasingly work through AI agents; AI agents need reliable interfaces, context, permissions, and tools; and partners determine where those experiences are discovered and adopted. You will make those three parts work together so MongoDB becomes the obvious database choice wherever AI-native software is created.
 The role is highly cross-functional and highly visible. You will work with engineering, design, IAM, billing, security, documentation, analytics, product marketing, partnerships, field teams, and strategic customers and partners. You will be expected to operate as both a strategic product leader and a hands-on builder who can turn an ambiguous ecosystem opportunity into a clear product vision, strategy, and an executable roadmap.
 What You’ll Do
 Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the MongoDB Partner Platform, starting with the Partner API and evolving toward a scalable, self-serve industry leading partner experience
 Turn partner and customer needs into clear product bets, sequencing near-term delivery against a compelling long-term platform strategy
 Build the next phases of the Partner API, including self-serve onboarding, enterprise and administrator controls, partner-managed account creation and billing, partner discovery, and a high-quality integration bar
 Establish a repeatable operating model for partner intake, design-partner engagement, integration support, launch readiness, documentation, incident response, and post-launch learning
 Partner deeply with the Partner team, IAM, Billing, Security, Engineering, Design, Docs, Analytics, Product Marketing, Sales, and Technical Services to align all towards the cross-functional outcomes required
